name: Tacoma
headline: Pierce County’s waterfront city on Commencement Bay.
lede: Tacoma is the county seat of Pierce County, about 30 miles south of Seattle on Commencement Bay. This guide covers getting around, parks, schools, everyday errands, neighborhoods and the towns close by, with every fact linked to its source.

chapters.title: Getting around and commutes
chapters.intro: Interstate 5 runs through Tacoma for about 6.5 miles, and State Route 16 carries traffic west to the Tacoma Narrows Bridge and the Kitsap Peninsula. Tacoma Dome Station, southeast of downtown, is the city’s main train and bus hub.
items: Sound Transit’s S Line runs weekdays from Tacoma Dome Station and South Tacoma Station to Seattle’s King Street Station; scheduled trips from Tacoma Dome take about 62 minutes.
Sound Transit Route 590 runs between Commerce Street Station and Tacoma Dome Station in Tacoma and downtown Seattle.
The T Line connects Tacoma Dome Station with downtown, the UW Tacoma campus and Hilltop. Its 2.4-mile Hilltop extension opened September 16, 2023, adding seven stations and running to St. Joseph.
Amtrak Cascades and Coast Starlight trains stop at Tacoma Dome Station.
The Stream Community Line runs between Tacoma Dome Station and Spanaway, with buses about every 20 minutes.
State Route 16 crosses the Narrows on twin spans opened in 1950 (westbound) and 2007 (eastbound).
Tolls are collected only on trips headed to Tacoma. For a two-axle vehicle: $4.50 with a Good To Go! pass, $5.50 at the toll booth, $6.50 by mail.

The Tacoma Dome Link Extension is in planning: about 8.5 miles with four new stations, including Fife, East Tacoma/Portland Avenue and Tacoma Dome. The Final EIS is expected in 2027; no opening year is posted.
Mean travel time to work for Tacoma residents is 28.8 minutes (2020–2024).

chapters.title: Parks and outdoors
chapters.intro: Metro Parks Tacoma manages 2,905 acres of parkland, from the old-growth forest at Point Defiance to the two-mile Ruston Way waterfront.
items: A 760-acre park at the city’s northern tip. It became a public park in 1888.
About 400 acres of Point Defiance Park is old-growth forest.
Inside the park; the zoo was founded in 1891 and the aquarium added in 1933.
A living history museum in Point Defiance Park, a replica of a 19th-century Hudson’s Bay Company trading post.
The outer loop is closed to motor vehicles and open to walkers and cyclists; the Square Trail around it is 4.6 miles and the Triangle Trail on the inner loop is 3.3 miles.
Point Defiance also holds Owen Beach, a rose garden begun in 1895 and a Japanese garden with a 1914 pagoda that was once a streetcar station.
About two miles of shoreline parks on Commencement Bay, with a paved path, fishing piers, beach access and viewpoints.
Along the path are Chinese Reconciliation Park, Jack Hyde Park, Hamilton Park, Dickman Mill Park and Marine Park.
An 11-acre waterfront park with the paved Frank Herbert Trail, named for the Tacoma-born author of Dune; the Wilson Way Bridge links it to Point Defiance Park and Ruston Way.

chapters.title: Schools
chapters.intro: Tacoma Public Schools serves about 28,000 students from preschool through grade 12, and its boundaries include almost all of Tacoma plus Ruston, Browns Point, Dash Point and parts of nearby cities. Boundaries change; confirm school assignment with the district for any specific address.
items: The district lists 36 elementary schools, 13 middle schools, 11 high schools and 4 early learning centers.
The district’s school boundaries page has an address lookup tool; Enrollment Services can be reached at 253-571-1000.
Options include the downtown School of the Arts (founded 2001) and the Science and Math Institute in Point Defiance Park (founded 2009).
Some Tacoma addresses fall in Clover Park, Fife, Franklin Pierce or University Place school districts.
University of Washington Tacoma began classes downtown in 1990 and grew into repurposed warehouses on the southern edge of downtown.

chapters.title: Everyday errands
chapters.intro: Several of Tacoma’s hospitals sit along the Hilltop’s “Medical Mile,” and the public library has eight locations across the city.
items: A 437-bed hospital that traces its start to 1882, attached to Mary Bridge Children’s Hospital.
St. Joseph and Tacoma General share Level II trauma care through the Tacoma Trauma Trust, alternating days.
MultiCare Allenmore Hospital and Mary Bridge Children’s Hospital are also in Tacoma.
Eight locations: Main, Fern Hill, Kobetich, Moore, Mottet, South Tacoma, Swasey and Wheelock. The Main Branch opened in 1903 as Washington’s first Carnegie library.
Saturdays at N. 27th and N. Proctor, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., April 4 through December 19, 2026, with winter dates in early 2027.
The Tacoma Farmers Market’s Broadway Market runs Thursdays at 9th and Broadway downtown; check the current season.

chapters.title: Housing and neighborhoods
chapters.intro: The City of Tacoma organizes neighborhoods into eight neighborhood council areas: Central, Eastside, New Tacoma, North End, Northeast, South End, South Tacoma and West End. In 2020–2024, 55.8% of housing units were owner-occupied, the median owner-occupied home value was $479,600 and median gross rent was $1,676.
items: A north end business district centered at Proctor Street and North 26th, home to the 1923 Blue Mouse Theatre and the Wheelock branch library.

A north end neighborhood named for historic Stadium High School, with homes, apartments and condominiums, some with Commencement Bay views; the Stadium-Seminary Historic District was listed on the National Register in 1985.
The site of the original settlement, where Job Carr built a cabin in 1865; St. Peter’s Church, the city’s oldest existing building, is here.
On a bluff above Commencement Bay, home to the Medical Mile hospitals and served by the T Line along Martin Luther King Jr. Way.
Downtown holds UW Tacoma, the Museum of Glass with its Bridge of Glass, the Tacoma Art Museum, America’s Car Museum and the Washington State History Museum.

chapters.title: What’s nearby
chapters.intro: Tacoma borders several smaller cities, and Seattle is about 30 miles north.
items: A separate town incorporated in 1906, surrounded on three sides by Tacoma; it includes the 97-acre Point Ruston development on the former smelter site. 1,055 people in 2020.
Across the Tacoma Narrows on Puget Sound, known as “the Maritime City.” 12,029 people in 2020.
Incorporated in 1995, home to the Chambers Bay golf course, host of the 2015 U.S. Open. 34,866 people in 2020.
An eastern neighbor on Interstate 5, entirely within the Puyallup Indian Reservation. 10,999 people in 2020.
About 10 miles southeast, home to the Washington State Fair and a Sounder stop. 42,973 people in 2020.
Pierce County’s second-largest city, bordering Joint Base Lewis–McChord, with the S Line’s southern terminus. 63,612 people in 2020.
Mount Rainier National Park is about 58 miles southeast.

faq: What is the population of Tacoma, WA?
219,346 at the 2020 census. The Census Bureau estimates 229,816 for July 1, 2025.
census
How far is Tacoma from Seattle?
About 30 miles.
wiki
How long does the Sounder train take from Tacoma to Seattle?
Scheduled weekday trips from Tacoma Dome Station to King Street Station take about 62 minutes. Sounder does not run on weekends.
st_sline
Where does the T Line go in Tacoma?
It runs from Tacoma Dome Station through downtown and UW Tacoma to Hilltop and St. Joseph. The 2.4-mile Hilltop extension opened September 16, 2023.
st_tline
Is light rail coming from Seattle to the Tacoma Dome?
The Tacoma Dome Link Extension from Federal Way is in planning, about 8.5 miles with four stations. Sound Transit expects the Final EIS in 2027 and has not posted an opening year.
st_tdle
How much is the Tacoma Narrows Bridge toll?
Only trips toward Tacoma are tolled. A two-axle vehicle pays $4.50 with a Good To Go! pass, $5.50 at the booth or $6.50 by mail.
wsdot_tnb
How big is Point Defiance Park?
760 acres, including about 400 acres of old-growth forest.
wiki_pd
Is Point Ruston in Tacoma?
Point Ruston sits on the former smelter site in the Town of Ruston, a separate municipality incorporated in 1906 and surrounded on three sides by Tacoma.
wiki_ruston
What school district is Tacoma in?

Most of the city is in Tacoma Public Schools, about 28,000 students. Some addresses are in Clover Park, Fife, Franklin Pierce or University Place districts. Boundaries change; confirm with the district for a specific address.
wiki
What is the median home value in Tacoma?
$479,600 for owner-occupied homes, per the Census Bureau’s 2020–2024 estimates. Median gross rent was $1,676.
census
When is the Proctor Farmers Market?
Saturdays, 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., April 4 through December 19, 2026, at N. 27th and N. Proctor Streets.
proctor_fm
What hospitals are in Tacoma?
MultiCare Tacoma General, St. Joseph Medical Center, Mary Bridge Children’s Hospital and MultiCare Allenmore Hospital.
